Day 78 of 100 · Kubernetes

Kubernetes Secrets

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityKubernetesPublished artifact recovered

Kubernetes Secrets provide a dedicated object for sensitive configuration, but confidentiality still depends on access control, storage protection and application behavior.

Architecture / mental model

Secret → env / projected volume → Pod
Secret object → etcd storage + RBAC/encryption controls

How it works

A Secret keeps sensitive values out of the Pod specification and container image. It can be created imperatively or declared with fields such as `stringData`, which Kubernetes converts into the encoded `data` representation.

Base64 is encoding, not encryption. Anyone with read access to the Secret can decode the value. Real credentials therefore do not become safe to commit merely because Kubernetes stores a base64 representation.

Secret-backed environment variables are read when the container starts. Mounted Secret volumes can receive updates eventually, while `subPath` mounts do not receive automatic updates.

Hands-on reference

kubectl create secret generic app-secret --from-literal=DB_USER=appuser --from-literal=DB_PASSWORD=change-me
kubectl get secret app-secret
kubectl describe secret app-secret
kubectl get secret app-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.DB_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d

Verification

Create only lab values, consume one through an environment variable and one through a volume, update the Secret and observe update behavior. Confirm an identity without Secret read permission cannot retrieve the object.

Field note / gotcha

Base64 ≠ encryption. Also, Secret env vars do not auto-update and `subPath` volume mounts do not receive projected updates.

Security considerations

Enable etcd encryption at rest where appropriate, apply least-privilege RBAC, rotate credentials, prevent apps from logging Secret contents and use external secret managers for higher-sensitivity environments when justified.

What I learned

Kubernetes gives secrets a dedicated delivery mechanism; it does not take responsibility for every layer of secret security.
